learn.title: Floating Solar Farms on Water
learn.intro: Floating solar farms are revolutionizing renewable energy by placing panels on reservoirs, reducing water evaporation while generating clean power. This innovation addresses land scarcity and supports water conservation, crucial for India's drought-prone regions and growing energy demands.
learn.c1_text: Panels on water stay cooler than land-based ones, boosting efficiency by 5-10%. Water naturally cools the panels, similar to how sweating cools humans. This synergy increases energy output without extra land use, making floating solar ideal for dense or arid regions.
learn.c3_title: 🇮🇳 India’s Push for Floating Solar Projects
learn.c3_text: India has launched over 100 floating solar projects, targeting 40 GW capacity by 2030. The 600 MW Ramagundam project in Telangana is among the largest. These installations support PM-KISAN and Jal Shakti missions by saving water and empowering rural communities.
learn.stat1: India plans 40 GW floating solar by 2030
learn.stat2: Floating panels reduce evaporation by up to 70%
learn.stat3: Panel efficiency increases by 5-10% on water
learn.stat4: Over 100 floating solar projects underway in India

learn.title: Geothermal Energy: Earth's Hidden Power
learn.intro: Geothermal energy taps into Earth’s internal heat for clean, reliable power and heating. Unlike solar or wind, it runs 24/7, offering baseload energy critical for India’s net-zero goals and energy security through sustainable thermal resources.
learn.c1_text: Geothermal energy harnesses heat from deep within Earth, formed by radioactive decay and planetary formation. Think of Earth as a giant furnace. This heat warms underground water, creating steam that spins turbines to generate electricity—clean and constant like a never-setting sun.
learn.c2_text: Geothermal plants drill into hot rock layers, using steam or hot water to drive turbines. Enhanced geothermal systems fracture hot dry rock to circulate fluid, similar to fracking but for heat. This method unlocks vast energy potential even in areas without natural reservoirs.
learn.c3_title: 🇮🇳 India’s Geothermal Potential in the Himalayas
learn.c3_text: India has 700 MW geothermal potential, mainly in the Himalayan region. The Geothermal Park in Himachal Pradesh explores this resource. With tectonic activity akin to Iceland, India could meet 10% of its renewable target via geothermal, supporting remote mountain electrification.
learn.stat3: Iceland generates 25% of its electricity from geothermal
learn.stat4: Himalayan states hold 90% of India’s geothermal reserves

learn.title: Bifacial Solar Panels Explained
learn.intro: Bifacial solar panels capture sunlight from both sides, increasing energy yield without expanding land use. This breakthrough boosts ROI for solar projects, especially in India where maximizing output per acre is vital for large-scale installations and rooftop programs.
learn.c1_text: Bifacial panels absorb light from both front and back, like wearing mirrored sunglasses that reflect and collect light. They generate 10-25% more power than traditional panels. The rear side captures reflected light from the ground, enhancing output even on cloudy days.
learn.c2_text: These panels use transparent backsheets or dual glass layers to allow light entry. Mounted on trackers or elevated structures, they optimize albedo—surface reflectivity. Snow, sand, or white surfaces beneath amplify gains, making them ideal for India’s varied terrain and agricultural lands.
learn.c3_text: India’s Bhadla Solar Park uses bifacial modules across 2 GW. The government promotes them under KUSUM scheme for higher farmer income. With manufacturing incentives under PLI, India aims to produce 500 GW renewables by 2030, leveraging bifacial tech for efficient land use.
learn.stat2: India targets 500 GW renewable capacity by 2030
learn.stat3: Bhadla Solar Park spans 14 GW with bifacial modules
learn.stat4: Global bifacial market expected to reach $23 billion by 2030

learn.title: Building Integrated Photovoltaics (BIPV)
learn.intro: Building Integrated Photovoltaics (BIPV) blend solar cells into building materials, turning facades and rooftops into power generators. This approach supports India’s smart city mission and urban decarbonization by merging aesthetics with clean energy.
learn.c1_text: BIPV replaces conventional building materials like roof tiles or curtain walls with energy-generating equivalents. Picture windows that power your home instead of just letting light in. This dual function reduces construction costs and energy bills, making buildings active participants in the grid.
learn.c2_text: BIPV comes in rooftop shingles, facades, skylights, and canopies. Tesla’s Solar Roof mimics slate tiles. In commercial spaces, glass-glass modules serve as atriums or balconies. These systems reduce HVAC loads due to shading, enhancing overall building performance and sustainability.
learn.c3_title: 🇮🇳 India’s Smart Cities and BIPV Vision
learn.c3_text: India’s Smart Cities Mission includes 100 cities integrating BIPV in public buildings. The Indira Gandhi International Airport uses solar-integrated roofing. With net metering policies in states like Gujarat, BIPV helps achieve 500 GW renewables by 2030 while modernizing urban infrastructure.
learn.stat1: BIPV can reduce building energy use by 30%
learn.stat2: India has 100 Smart Cities slated for green upgrades
learn.stat3: Global BIPV market projected to hit $68 billion by 2030
learn.stat4: IGI Airport Delhi features 2.6 MW rooftop solar integration

learn.title: Solar PV and the Photoelectric Effect
learn.intro: The photoelectric effect powers solar panels, converting sunlight directly into electricity. Understanding this quantum phenomenon helps students and professionals grasp how solar PV systems work, supporting India’s solar expansion and global clean energy transition.
learn.c1_text: When photons strike a solar cell, they knock electrons loose from silicon atoms, like raindrops dislodging marbles. This flow of electrons creates direct current (DC), captured by metal contacts on the panel surface. The effect was first explained by Einstein, winning him the Nobel Prize.
learn.c2_title: 🔋 From DC to Usable AC Power
learn.c2_text: Solar panels produce DC power, which inverters convert to alternating current (AC) for homes and grids. Each cell generates about 0.5 volts. Panels are wired in series/parallel to boost voltage/current. This modular design allows scalable systems from rooftops to utility farms.
learn.c3_title: 🇮🇳 India’s Solar Growth Powered by PV Tech
learn.c3_text: India’s 76 GW solar capacity (2024) relies on photoelectric tech. The National Solar Mission aims for 280 GW by 2030. JNNSM boosted manufacturing and R&D, driving down tariffs. Innovations like PERC and TOPCon cells further improve efficiency, reinforcing India’s leadership in solar adoption.

learn.stat2: Each solar cell produces approximately 0.5 volts
learn.stat3: Einstein won Nobel Prize for explaining photoelectric effect

learn.title: Iron-Air Batteries for Grid Storage
learn.intro: Iron-air batteries offer long-duration energy storage, storing power for 100+ hours using abundant iron. This technology could transform India’s grid reliability, enabling renewable integration and reducing dependence on lithium imports for large-scale storage.
learn.c1_text: Iron-air batteries store energy by rusting iron, then reversing the process to release it—like burning steel wool backwards. They use cheap, non-flammable materials. With 100+ hour discharge cycles, they outlast lithium-ion batteries, ideal for seasonal storage and grid balancing.
learn.c2_text: These batteries use iron, air, and water—materials costing under $5/kWh. Unlike lithium, iron is abundant and non-toxic. Form Energy commercializes them with regenerative fuel cells. Their slow discharge suits grid-scale needs, offering weeks of backup power without rare earth elements or fire risks.
learn.c3_text: India’s grid needs 40 GWh storage by 2030. Iron-air batteries could fill gaps during monsoons or heatwaves. Startups like Gegadyne are testing similar tech. Government supports via STORAGE mission, aiming to reduce lithium import reliance and stabilize renewables-dependent grids.
learn.stat1: Iron-air batteries store energy for 100+ hours
learn.stat2: Material cost under $5/kWh vs $150+/kWh for lithium
learn.stat3: India needs 40 GWh grid storage by 2030
learn.stat4: Iron constitutes 5% of Earth’s crust—abundant resource
